<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Part of #31479. Enables tower + connector LoRA for **Voxtral**, reworked on top of the `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` interface merged in #42662 (which replaced the two token-count helpers this PR originally added). Addresses all three of @linitra24's review findings.

## Claims

- `AudioLanguageAdapter.w_in` / `w_out` are converted from `nn.Linear` to `ReplicatedLinear`, so the connector is actually LoRA-wrappable (`from_layer` previously left plain `nn.Linear` unwrapped). Parameter names are unchanged, so existing checkpoints and adapter target names keep resolving.
- `get_mm_lora_token_counts` is implemented for Voxtral's chunked encoder path: at runtime the chunk count is derived from the item's padded audio in `mm_kwargs`, so `tower_tokens = num_chunks * max_source_positions` equals the exact M the whisper tower forwards (punica's `token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` holds). The `mm_kwargs=None` path (punica wrapper sizing, encoder-cache-served items) ceils `num_mm_embeds` to whole 30-second chunks, fixing the under-allocation in the review example: budget 16384 now sizes 44 chunks → 66000 rows, not `16384 * 4 = 65536`.
- `VoxtralRealtimeGeneration` opts out (`supports_tower_connector_lora = False`): its streaming processor skips chunk padding and builds placeholders from raw sample counts, so the chunk-derived counts would not hold there.

## Validation

Run on an A100 (nightly `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev376+g5555a2d8f`, `torch 2.13.0+cu129`) with the modules from this diff:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_voxtral.py -v
test_mm_lora_token_counts_match_processor_output[mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507] PASSED
test_adapter_linears_are_lora_wrappable PASSED
2 passed in 6.41s
```

Lint: `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` (pinned v0.14.0) pass on the three changed files.

The new test exercises the supported path rather than helper arithmetic: it runs the real Voxtral multimodal processor on synthetic audios of awkward lengths and asserts the hook's runtime counts against the processor's actual chunk-padded outputs, that the cache-served path (`mm_kwargs=None` with the item's placeholder count) returns identical counts, and that the sizing call upper-bounds the runtime totals — including the non-multiple-of-375 budget case (`num_mm_embeds=16384` → `(66000, 16384)`), which fails under the old formula. A second test asserts the adapter linears are vLLM-native and LoRA-wrappable with stable parameter names.

Pending before `ready`: end-to-end LoRA inference on GPU with an adapter targeting `whisper_encoder` + `audio_language_adapter.{w_in,w_out}` (multi-item, multi-chunk batch), and a load check of a quantized mistral-format checkpoint now that `quant_config` is threaded into the adapter. I'll post both here.

## Details

- Runtime vs sizing is the split #42662 was designed for: sizing needs an upper bound from the encoder budget, runtime needs exact per-item counts, and Voxtral's independent per-item 30s padding means the two cannot be computed from one formula. `connector_tokens = num_mm_embeds` on both paths because the adapter consumes exactly one row per LM audio embed (see `embed_multimodal`).
- The exactness of the cache-served path relies on the feature extractor padding audio to whole 30s chunks before placeholder counting, making every placeholder count a multiple of `ceil(max_source_positions / downsample_factor) = 375`.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR implements `get_mm_lora_token_counts` or connector conversion for Voxtral (checked `gh pr list --search "voxtral lora"` / `"get_mm_lora_token_counts"`; the active tower/connector PRs cover GLM-ASR #53149, Phi-4 #54832, Nemotron #58658, Whisper #59558 — different models).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this rework. I reviewed every changed line; the test commands and results above are from my own runs.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

@jeejeelee — a note on tower vs connector for this model, since they behave differently:

- **Tower (`whisper_encoder`)** is vLLM's native `WhisperEncoder` (QKV/Column/Row-parallel, including the explicit `MergedColumnParallelLinear` K/V split the code comments call out as enabling LoRA), so tower LoRA attaches and `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` is load-bearing — the whisper encoder runs at `downsample_factor`× the LM-visible audio tokens, which is the length the tower mapping needs.

- **Connector (`audio_language_adapter`)** currently uses plain `nn.Linear` (`w_in`/`w_out`). `from_layer` only wraps vLLM-native linear types, so connector LoRA is inert today: `get_num_mm_connector_tokens` still sizes the connector punica wrapper correctly, but it governs zero modules — no error, just a no-op.

`AudioLanguageAdapter` is small and self-contained, so converting `w_in`/`w_out` to `ReplicatedLinear` would make connector LoRA actually attach. Happy to fold that into this PR, or keep this scoped to the tower + token-count helpers and do the connector conversion as a follow-up — whichever you'd prefer.

Small correction to my "no-op" wording above — vLLM's adapter loader is stricter than that. `check_unexpected_modules` (`vllm/lora/lora_model.py`) rejects an adapter outright if it carries weights for any module not in the model's supported LoRA set; I confirmed on a GPU that targeting `nn.Linear` audio modules raises `ValueError: ... expected target modules {...} but received [...]`, rather than silently skipping. So a tower-only adapter loads fine, but an adapter that includes `audio_language_adapter` weights would error at load.

That makes the `w_in`/`w_out` → `ReplicatedLinear` swap more than cosmetic — it's what lets a tower+connector adapter load at all. Happy to fold it into this PR if you'd like connector LoRA to be usable.

@jeejeelee gentle ping — is there anything you'd like changed here before it gets a `ready` label so CI can run? Scope is unchanged (the two token-count helpers + CPU test). If it helps, I can also fold the connector → `ReplicatedLinear` conversion from the #45771 discussion into this PR rather than keeping it as a follow-up.

@linitra24 thanks for the review — all three findings were right, and the PR is reworked from scratch on top of #42662 (which merged while this sat and is the designed fix for the sizing/runtime split you pointed out). Summary of the new shape, with details in the updated description and inline replies:

- `AudioLanguageAdapter.w_in`/`w_out` → `ReplicatedLinear`, so connector LoRA actually wraps (your first comment).
- `get_mm_lora_token_counts` replaces the old helpers: runtime counts come from the item's padded audio in `mm_kwargs` (exact whisper M per item), the `mm_kwargs=None` sizing path ceils the budget to whole 30s chunks — your 16384-budget example now sizes 66000, matching the real M, instead of 65536 (your second comment).
- The arithmetic-only test is gone; the replacement drives the real Voxtral multimodal processor and checks the hook against what the processor actually produced, including the non-multiple-of-375 budget case that the old formula fails (your third comment).
- `VoxtralRealtimeGeneration` opts out via `supports_tower_connector_lora = False` — its streaming processor skips chunk padding, so the chunk-derived counts would not hold there.

Both new tests pass on an A100 against the current nightly (`0.31.1rc1.dev376`), including the processor-driven count checks — command and output in the updated description.

Still pending before this is `ready`: an end-to-end GPU run with an adapter targeting the tower + adapter modules, and a quantized-checkpoint load check (since `quant_config` is now threaded into the adapter) — I'll post both here.

Both pending validations are done, on the same A100 / nightly `v0.31.1rc1.dev376+g5555a2d8f` setup as the unit tests above (this branch's `voxtral.py`/`voxtral_realtime.py` overlaid onto the nightly's site-packages, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`).

**1. End-to-end LoRA run over the tower + connector — passed, and the first attempt caught a real sizing bug, now fixed in c553427.**

Setup: a synthetic rank-8 PEFT adapter targeting every whisper-encoder layer's `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`/`out_proj`/`fc1`/`fc2` plus `audio_language_adapter.w_in`/`w_out`, and a three-prompt batch of synthetic audios of 8.3 s / 45 s / 70.1 s (1 / 2 / 3 whisper chunks, none chunk-aligned), prompts built with `mistral_common` `AudioChunk`s:

```python
llm = vllm.LLM(
    model="mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507",
    tokenizer_mode="mistral", config_format="mistral", load_format="mistral",
    enable_lora=True, max_loras=1, max_lora_rank=8,
    enable_tower_connector_lora=True,
    mm_processor_cache_gb=0, max_model_len=4096,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.2, enforce_eager=True,
)
```

Three greedy generations over the batch: no adapter, an adapter with `lora_B = 0` (LoRA delta exactly zero), and one with random `lora_B`:

```
[base]       prompt 0: 'The audio consists of a continuous, high-pitched humming sound, which is typical of a motor or machinery running.'
[lora-zeroB] prompt 0: (byte-identical to base, all 3 prompts)
[lora-randB] prompt 0: 'The audio consists of a continuous, high-pitched whirring sound, which is likely a representation of a machine or'
CHECK zero-B == base: PASS (outputs identical)
CHECK rand-B changes outputs (adapter actually applied): True
=== E2E SMOKE TEST PASSED ===
```

Zero `could not be wrapped` / unexpected-module warnings in the log, and the random-B run shows the adapter is actually applied through the tower and connector, not silently ignored.

The bug the first run caught: engine init crashed before any request, in the encoder-cache profiling pass, inside the wrapped connector `ReplicatedLinear` forward:

```
File ".../vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", line 291, in _lora_shrink
    assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
AssertionError
```

The `mm_kwargs=None` sizing path returned the raw budget (8192) as the connector count, but encoder profiling batches maximum-size items whose embeds are chunk-padded: with `max_model_len=4096`, each dummy audio spans 11 chunks = 4125 embeds, and the two profiled items run 8250 connector rows > 8192. The tower count was already chunk-ceiled (`ceil(8192/375) = 22` chunks → 33000 ≥ 2 × 11 × 1500), which is why only the connector tripped. The fix chunk-ceils the connector count the same way (`ceil(budget/375) * 375`); exact per-item counts at runtime and for cache-served items (always whole chunks) are unchanged. Force-pushed as c553427, and the processor-driven tests were updated (the 16384-budget case now expects a 16500 connector bound) and re-run on the box:

```
python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_voxtral.py -v
tests/models/multimodal/test_voxtral.py::test_mm_lora_token_counts_match_processor_output[mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507] PASSED
tests/models/multimodal/test_voxtral.py::test_adapter_linears_are_lora_wrappable PASSED
======================== 2 passed, 14 warnings in 5.95s ========================
```

**2. Quantized-checkpoint load check — passed on a real FP8 mistral-format checkpoint.**

`RedHatAI/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-FP8-dynamic` is compressed-tensors FP8-dynamic in mistral format: LM linears quantized, with every whisper-encoder linear and `mm_whisper_embeddings.audio_language_projection.{0,2}` on the `ignore` list — exactly what the `quant_config` threading has to get right, since the remapped ignore list must now reach the adapter's `ReplicatedLinear`s instead of plain `nn.Linear`s. Loaded with the same mistral-format args (no LoRA flags needed for this check); `load_weights` succeeds, and inspecting the live model:

```
audio_language_adapter.w_in:  ReplicatedLinear, quant_method=UnquantizedLinearMethod, weight dtype=torch.bfloat16
audio_language_adapter.w_out: ReplicatedLinear, quant_method=UnquantizedLinearMethod, weight dtype=torch.bfloat16
whisper_encoder.whisper_encoder.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj: QKVParallelLinear, quant_method=UnquantizedLinearMethod, weight dtype=torch.bfloat16
language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj: QKVParallelLinear, quant_method=CompressedTensorsLinearMethod, weight dtype=torch.int32
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj: MergedColumnParallelLinear, quant_method=CompressedTensorsLinearMethod, weight dtype=torch.int32
```

An audio generate on the FP8 checkpoint runs through the adapter forward and is coherent (`'This is a sound effect of a bell ringing.'`):

```
=== FP8 LOAD CHECK PASSED ===
```

That closes out both items pending from the rework; ready for another look.

`AudioLanguageAdapter` still uses plain nn.Linear, which cannot be wrapped by vLLM's LoRA implementation. It looks like this PR only adds the connector token mapping, but does not actually enable connector LoRA. Should w_in and w_out be converted to ReplicatedLinear as part of this PR?

This is incorrect for Voxtral's chunked encoder path. get_num_mm_encoder_tokens is not only called with the placeholder count of an already-processed item; LoRAModelManager also calls it with the total encoder budget.
With max_model_len=8192 and two audio items, the manager allocates 16384 * 4 = 65536 tower mapping entries. However, Voxtral pads each audio independently to 30-second chunks, so each 8192-token dummy audio becomes 8250 tokens. The Whisper tower therefore receives [44, 1500, hidden], i.e. M=66000, and inference reliably fails at:
```
assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
```

You're right, and this is what the rework fixes. The branch is rebuilt on top of #42662, which replaced the two helpers with a single `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality, mm_kwargs, num_mm_embeds)` hook that receives the item's processed `mm_kwargs` at runtime and `mm_kwargs=None` with the encoder budget when `LoRAModelManager` sizes the punica wrappers.

Runtime: the chunk count comes from the item's padded audio array (`ceil(num_samples / chunk_samples)`, mirroring `VoxtralEncoderModel.prepare_inputs_for_conv`), and `tower_tokens = num_chunks * max_source_positions` — the exact M the whisper tower forwards for that item. `connector_tokens = num_mm_embeds`, since the adapter consumes exactly one row per LM audio embed (see `embed_multimodal`).

Sizing: with `mm_kwargs=None` the count is derived from `num_mm_embeds` by ceiling to whole 30-second chunks (`tokens_per_chunk = ceil(max_source_positions / downsample_factor)` = 375).

For your example: each 8192-token dummy audio is padded to 22 chunks (8250 tokens), so the tower sees [44, 1500, hidden] for the two items, M = 44 * 1500 = 66000. The sizing call now allocates ceil(16384 / 375) = 44 chunks → 66000 mapping entries instead of 16384 * 4 = 65536, so `token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` holds with 66000 on both sides. Since the feature extractor pads before placeholder counting, every item's placeholder count is a multiple of 375, which makes the budget-derived bound cover any scheduled batch. The new test pins your exact case: `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality="audio", mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=16384) == (66000, 16384)`, which fails under the old formula. The new tests — including this exact 16384 case — pass on an A100 against the current nightly; the end-to-end punica-assert run with a real adapter is pending and will be posted here.

+import contextlib
+import math
+import os
+import tempfile
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.multimodal import MultiModalDummyOptions
+from vllm.distributed import (
+    cleanup_dist_env_and_memory,
+    init_distributed_environment,
+    initialize_model_parallel,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import ReplicatedLinear
+from vllm.model_executor.models.voxtral import (
+    AudioLanguageAdapter,
+    VoxtralForConditionalGeneration,
+)
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+
+from ...utils import ensure_current_vllm_config
+from ..utils import build_model_context
+
+
+class _StubModel:
+    """Carries only the attributes `get_mm_lora_token_counts` reads from
+    `self`, so the real method can be exercised without constructing the
+    full model (whisper tower, language model, etc.)."""
+
+    get_mm_lora_token_counts = VoxtralForConditionalGeneration.get_mm_lora_token_counts
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_id", ["mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507"])
+def test_mm_lora_token_counts_match_processor_output(model_id):
+    """The LoRA token counts must match what the whisper tower and adapter
+    actually process: the real processor pads each audio independently to
+    whole 30-second chunks, so the tower token count cannot be derived by
+    scaling the placeholder count of an unpadded audio."""
+    ctx = build_model_context(model_id, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 2})
+    model_config = ctx.model_config
+    processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config)
+    feature_extractor = processor.info.get_feature_extractor()
+    sr = feature_extractor.sampling_rate
+
+    mistral_audio_config = feature_extractor.audio_encoder.audio_config
+    chunk_samples = int(mistral_audio_config.chunk_length_s * sr)
+
+    audio_config = model_config.hf_config.audio_config
+    tokens_per_chunk = math.ceil(
+        audio_config.max_source_positions / audio_config.downsample_factor
+    )
+
+    stub = _StubModel()
+    stub.config = model_config.hf_config
+    stub.downsample_factor = audio_config.downsample_factor
+    # Mel frames per 30-second chunk, as `VoxtralEncoderModel.chunk_size`
+    # derives from its conv strides.
+    stub.whisper_encoder = SimpleNamespace(
+        chunk_size=chunk_samples // audio_config.hop_length
+    )
+
+    # Awkward lengths: not aligned to the 30-second chunk or the token frame;
+    # the second audio spans multiple chunks.
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
+    audios = [
+        rng.rand(int(7.3 * sr)).astype(np.float32),
+        rng.rand(int(41.7 * sr)).astype(np.float32),
+    ]
+    mm_data = {"audio": [(audio, sr) for audio in audios]}
+
+    token_prompt = processor.get_dummy_inputs(
+        model_config.max_model_len,
+        {"audio": len(audios)},
+        mm_options=MultiModalDummyOptions(),
+        mm_data=mm_data,
+    ).prompt
+    mm_input = processor(
+        token_prompt,
+        mm_items=processor.info.parse_mm_data(mm_data),
+        hf_processor_mm_kwargs={},
+    )
+
+    mm_items = mm_input["mm_kwargs"]["audio"]
+    placeholders = mm_input["mm_placeholders"]["audio"]
+    assert len(mm_items) == len(placeholders) == len(audios)
+
+    runtime_counts = []
+    for mm_item, placeholder, audio in zip(mm_items, placeholders, audios):
+        num_embeds = placeholder.get_num_embeds()
+        padded_len = len(mm_item.get_data()["audio_arrays"])
+        assert padded_len >= len(audio)
+        assert padded_len % chunk_samples == 0
+        num_chunks = padded_len // chunk_samples
+
+        tower_tokens, connector_tokens = stub.get_mm_lora_token_counts(
+            modality="audio", mm_kwargs=mm_item, num_mm_embeds=num_embeds
+        )
+        # The whisper tower runs every padded chunk at full context; the
+        # adapter consumes one row per LM audio embed.
+        assert tower_tokens == num_chunks * audio_config.max_source_positions
+        assert connector_tokens == num_embeds
+        assert num_embeds == num_chunks * tokens_per_chunk
+
+        # An item served from the encoder cache (mm_kwargs=None) must get
+        # the same exact counts.
+        assert stub.get_mm_lora_token_counts(
+            modality="audio", mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=num_embeds
+        ) == (tower_tokens, connector_tokens)
+
+        runtime_counts.append((tower_tokens, connector_tokens))
+
+    # Wrapper sizing (LoRAModelManager passes the encoder budget with
+    # mm_kwargs=None) must bound the runtime counts of any batch within
+    # that budget.
+    budget = sum(placeholder.get_num_embeds() for placeholder in placeholders)
+    sizing_tower, sizing_connector = stub.get_mm_lora_token_counts(
+        modality="audio", mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=budget
+    )
+    assert sizing_tower >= sum(tower for tower, _ in runtime_counts)
+    assert sizing_connector >= sum(conn for _, conn in runtime_counts)
+
+    # The real encoder budget is not a multiple of tokens_per_chunk (375
+    # here), so both bounds must round up to whole chunks: 16384 embeds
+    # span 44 chunks of 1500 tower tokens and 44 * 375 = 16500 connector
+    # rows. Scaling the tower by downsample_factor instead would
+    # under-allocate (16384 * 4 = 65536 < 66000), and returning the raw
+    # budget for the connector would too: encoder profiling batches
+    # maximum-size items whose embeds are chunk-padded, so an 8192-token
+    # budget profiled with two 4096-embed items runs 2 * 4125 = 8250
+    # connector rows.
+    assert tokens_per_chunk == 375
+    assert stub.get_mm_lora_token_counts(
+        modality="audio", mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=16384
+    ) == (66000, 16500)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def dist_init():
+    fd, temp_file = tempfile.mkstemp()
+    os.close(fd)
+    try:
+        with ensure_current_vllm_config():
+            init_distributed_environment(
+                world_size=1,
+                rank=0,
+                distributed_init_method=f"file://{temp_file}",
+                local_rank=0,
+                backend="gloo",
+            )
+            initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+            yield
+        cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+    finally:
+        with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
+            os.unlink(temp_file)
+
+
+def test_adapter_linears_are_lora_wrappable(dist_init) -> None:
+    # vllm.lora.utils.from_layer only wraps vLLM-native linear layers, so the
+    # connector must use ReplicatedLinear for LoRA adapters targeting
+    # audio_language_adapter.{w_in,w_out} to load.
+    adapter = AudioLanguageAdapter(hidden_size=8, dim=4)
+    assert isinstance(adapter.w_in, ReplicatedLinear)
+    assert isinstance(adapter.w_out, ReplicatedLinear)
+
+    # Checkpoint remapping in load_weights relies on these parameter names.
+    assert {name for name, _ in adapter.named_parameters()} == {
+        "w_in.weight",
+        "w_out.weight",
+    }
+
+    for layer in (adapter.w_in, adapter.w_out):
+        layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+    out = adapter(torch.randn(3, 8))
+    assert out.shape == (3, 4)

+    def get_mm_lora_token_counts(
+        self,
+        *,
+        modality: str,
+        mm_kwargs: MultiModalKwargsItem | None,
+        num_mm_embeds: int,
+    ) -> tuple[int, int | None]:
+        """Return ``(tower_tokens, connector_tokens)`` for multimodal LoRA.
+
+        The feature extractor pads every audio independently to whole
+        30-second chunks, so the whisper tower always runs on
+        ``num_chunks * max_source_positions`` tokens per item, while the
+        adapter consumes exactly one row per LM audio embed (see
+        ``embed_multimodal``).
+
+        With ``mm_kwargs``, the chunk count is derived from the item's padded
+        audio array, mirroring ``VoxtralEncoderModel.prepare_inputs_for_conv``.
+        Without it (punica wrapper sizing from the encoder budget, or an item
+        served from the encoder cache), both counts are ceiled to whole
+        chunks: every scheduled item contributes chunk-padded embeds, so a
+        batch within an unaligned budget can exceed the raw budget (encoder
+        profiling runs ``ceil(budget / item_embeds)`` maximum-size items).
+        """
+        del modality
+        audio_config = self.config.audio_config
+        if mm_kwargs is not None:
+            audio_arr = mm_kwargs.get_data()["audio_arrays"]
+            chunk_samples = self.whisper_encoder.chunk_size * audio_config.hop_length
+            num_chunks = math.ceil(len(audio_arr) / chunk_samples)
+            return num_chunks * audio_config.max_source_positions, num_mm_embeds
+        tokens_per_chunk = math.ceil(
+            audio_config.max_source_positions / self.downsample_factor
+        )
+        num_chunks = math.ceil(num_mm_embeds / tokens_per_chunk)
+        return (
+            num_chunks * audio_config.max_source_positions,
+            num_chunks * tokens_per_chunk,
+        )

inline_comments.body:
This is incorrect for Voxtral's chunked encoder path. get_num_mm_encoder_tokens is not only called with the placeholder count of an already-processed item; LoRAModelManager also calls it with the total encoder budget.
With max_model_len=8192 and two audio items, the manager allocates 16384 * 4 = 65536 tower mapping entries. However, Voxtral pads each audio independently to 30-second chunks, so each 8192-token dummy audio becomes 8250 tokens. The Whisper tower therefore receives [44, 1500, hidden], i.e. M=66000, and inference reliably fails at:
```
assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
```

inline_comments.body:
You're right, and this is what the rework fixes. The branch is rebuilt on top of #42662, which replaced the two helpers with a single `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality, mm_kwargs, num_mm_embeds)` hook that receives the item's processed `mm_kwargs` at runtime and `mm_kwargs=None` with the encoder budget when `LoRAModelManager` sizes the punica wrappers.

Runtime: the chunk count comes from the item's padded audio array (`ceil(num_samples / chunk_samples)`, mirroring `VoxtralEncoderModel.prepare_inputs_for_conv`), and `tower_tokens = num_chunks * max_source_positions` — the exact M the whisper tower forwards for that item. `connector_tokens = num_mm_embeds`, since the adapter consumes exactly one row per LM audio embed (see `embed_multimodal`).

Sizing: with `mm_kwargs=None` the count is derived from `num_mm_embeds` by ceiling to whole 30-second chunks (`tokens_per_chunk = ceil(max_source_positions / downsample_factor)` = 375).

For your example: each 8192-token dummy audio is padded to 22 chunks (8250 tokens), so the tower sees [44, 1500, hidden] for the two items, M = 44 * 1500 = 66000. The sizing call now allocates ceil(16384 / 375) = 44 chunks → 66000 mapping entries instead of 16384 * 4 = 65536, so `token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` holds with 66000 on both sides. Since the feature extractor pads before placeholder counting, every item's placeholder count is a multiple of 375, which makes the budget-derived bound cover any scheduled batch. The new test pins your exact case: `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality="audio", mm_kwargs=None, num_mm_embeds=16384) == (66000, 16384)`, which fails under the old formula. The new tests — including this exact 16384 case — pass on an A100 against the current nightly; the end-to-end punica-assert run with a real adapter is pending and will be posted here.

@jeejeelee — a note on tower vs connector for this model, since they behave differently:

- **Tower (`whisper_encoder`)** is vLLM's native `WhisperEncoder` (QKV/Column/Row-parallel, including the explicit `MergedColumnParallelLinear` K/V split the code comments call out as enabling LoRA), so tower LoRA attaches and `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` is load-bearing — the whisper encoder runs at `downsample_factor`× the LM-visible audio tokens, which is the length the tower mapping needs.

- **Connector (`audio_language_adapter`)** currently uses plain `nn.Linear` (`w_in`/`w_out`). `from_layer` only wraps vLLM-native linear types, so connector LoRA is inert today: `get_num_mm_connector_tokens` still sizes the connector punica wrapper correctly, but it governs zero modules — no error, just a no-op.

`AudioLanguageAdapter` is small and self-contained, so converting `w_in`/`w_out` to `ReplicatedLinear` would make connector LoRA actually attach. Happy to fold that into this PR, or keep this scoped to the tower + token-count helpers and do the connector conversion as a follow-up — whichever you'd prefer.

Small correction to my "no-op" wording above — vLLM's adapter loader is stricter than that. `check_unexpected_modules` (`vllm/lora/lora_model.py`) rejects an adapter outright if it carries weights for any module not in the model's supported LoRA set; I confirmed on a GPU that targeting `nn.Linear` audio modules raises `ValueError: ... expected target modules {...} but received [...]`, rather than silently skipping. So a tower-only adapter loads fine, but an adapter that includes `audio_language_adapter` weights would error at load.

That makes the `w_in`/`w_out` → `ReplicatedLinear` swap more than cosmetic — it's what lets a tower+connector adapter load at all. Happy to fold it into this PR if you'd like connector LoRA to be usable.

@jeejeelee gentle ping — is there anything you'd like changed here before it gets a `ready` label so CI can run? Scope is unchanged (the two token-count helpers + CPU test). If it helps, I can also fold the connector → `ReplicatedLinear` conversion from the #45771 discussion into this PR rather than keeping it as a follow-up.

@linitra24 thanks for the review — all three findings were right, and the PR is reworked from scratch on top of #42662 (which merged while this sat and is the designed fix for the sizing/runtime split you pointed out). Zero `could not be wrapped` / unexpected-module warnings in the log, and the random-B run shows the adapter is actually applied through the tower and connector, not silently ignored.

The bug the first run caught: engine init crashed before any request, in the encoder-cache profiling pass, inside the wrapped connector `ReplicatedLinear` forward:

```
File ".../vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", line 291, in _lora_shrink
    assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
AssertionError
```

The `mm_kwargs=None` sizing path returned the raw budget (8192) as the connector count, but encoder profiling batches maximum-size items whose embeds are chunk-padded: with `max_model_len=4096`, each dummy audio spans 11 chunks = 4125 embeds, and the two profiled items run 8250 connector rows > 8192. The tower count was already chunk-ceiled (`ceil(8192/375) = 22` chunks → 33000 ≥ 2 × 11 × 1500), which is why only the connector tripped. The fix chunk-ceils the connector count the same way (`ceil(budget/375) * 375`); exact per-item counts at runtime and for cache-served items (always whole chunks) are unchanged.
